hero.headline: We put artificial intelligence to work inside your operation.
hero.sub: Osppy is an applied-AI company from Guadalajara. Applied means this: a concrete task, a written process, a system that does it on its own, and a result you review.
hero.ctaMessage: Hi, I'd like to talk about my business operations.

diagrama.pie: The step almost nobody has written down is the second one.
diagrama.alt: Four-step diagram: the task goes through a process written by someone, an agent carries it out, and it produces a result.

somos.headline: Systems running in real businesses today.
somos.p1: Osppy is an applied artificial-intelligence company from Guadalajara. We work with businesses of every size that want to use AI with judgment: to remove repetitive work, bring order to the operation, and stop everything from depending on the owner.
somos.p2: Osppy's systems run in real businesses today. What we recommend doesn't come from a conference stage: it comes from building, delivering, and keeping systems running.
somos.p3: There are three ways into an operation: train the team, advise on where AI is worth it — and where it isn't — and implement systems that stay running.
somos.cita: Artificial intelligence proposes. A person reviews and decides.
somos.citaNota: The principle behind everything we build.

capacitacion.body: Hands-on workshops for owners and teams: you leave able to apply something today, working on real tasks from your business. First we teach people to use the tools well; then we watch which problems keep coming back.
capacitacion.f3Value: The intro talk and the first workshop are written; the first groups are about to open
capacitacion.f4Value: Quoted per group and per outcome

asesoria.body: Sessions on how to make AI useful in your business. The first one is almost always a diagnostic: understanding your operation and finding where we can help. Sometimes the answer is training; sometimes it's putting a process in order; sometimes it's building.
asesoria.preguntasTitulo: The diagnostic starts with questions like:
preguntas: Where does your team's time actually go?
Which process repeats the same way every week?
What information do you already have that nobody is using?
What's worth automating — and what isn't yet?

implementacion.body: We build systems that stay running inside your operation — from a quoting tool to an agent that does the whole task on its own — with scope and success criteria in writing. After delivery, there are hosting, monitoring, and maintenance plans.
tipos: Models in your own infrastructure, with Amazon Bedrock

ayudamos.headline: Businesses with an operation you can describe.
ayudamos.body: We work with enterprises and businesses of every size. There is delivered work in these industries:
ayudamos.fraseCasa: …and any industry with an operation you can describe.

como.headline: Understand first. Building comes last.
como.p1Body: We get to know your operation and find where AI genuinely helps — and where it isn't needed.
como.p2Body: Before anything gets built, the process gets written down. It's the step almost nobody has done, and everything else depends on it.
como.p3Body: Quoted separately, with scope and success criteria in writing. No promises of savings, sales, or hours: the impact is measured by your numbers.
como.p4Body: What we deliver can stay under a hosting, monitoring, and maintenance plan, depending on what your operation needs.

trayectoria.headline: What has been done.
trayectoria.agentes: Also: agents that do the whole task on their own — autonomous — running in production systems today.
trayectoria.nota: “+100” and “+50” are the operator's own estimate as of 2026-09-02; no formal records exist for that stage.

casos.headline: The work can be told without names.
casos.body: No client is named here without written permission, and no figure is published without measurement. What we can say: the kind of work that has been delivered.
casos.t1Body: Systems that put a quote together using the business's own rules and prices, so it doesn't depend on one person.
casos.t2Body: They do a whole task on their own — autonomous — inside a defined process, with written rules.
casos.t3Body: They answer and attend with the information the business loads. If something isn't there, they say so or ask — they don't make things up.
casos.t4Body: Getting a whole team working with an enterprise-grade AI tool, with order and rules of use.
casos.t5Body: When the information can't leave your house, the model is deployed inside your own infrastructure, with Amazon Bedrock.
casos.t6Body: The groundwork: getting the process written down before automating anything. Without it, we don't build agents.
casos.t7Body: A diagnostic of the operation and a map of where AI helps — and where it doesn't.
casos.giros: Delivered across industries like construction, logistics, furniture stores, retail, private schools, and online businesses.

productos.headline: Two products, each with its own page.
productos.body: Besides services, Osppy builds products: the same conversational assistant on WhatsApp, one industry at a time.

hoteles.body: Diana answers guests on WhatsApp with the hotel's own information, and the team sees everything and operates from a panel. It's Osppy's assistant for hotels, and it operates today in hotels in production.

citas.body: Diana, for appointment-based businesses: clinics, practices, spas. It's under construction, with no committed date; we're looking for founding clinics.

testimonios.headline: Illustrative voices from people who use an assistant like this.
testimonios.nota: Quotes without names and without figures: they illustrate what it's like to have an assistant answering. They are not verified testimonials.
testimonios.q1: I used to answer messages at midnight every single day. Now I sleep. The assistant replies in my tone, with my business's exact information.
testimonios.q2: I thought a bot would feel fake. Not at all: my clients write to it the same way they write to me, and it knows when to hand the conversation over.
testimonios.q3: I stopped losing bookings to slow replies. What comes in overnight no longer goes unanswered.

faq.headline: What we usually get asked.
faq.a1: That artificial intelligence doesn't stay in a demo. It goes to work inside the operation: a concrete task, from a concrete role, with a result someone reviews.
faq.a2: Almost always with a diagnostic: understanding your operation and finding where AI genuinely helps. What follows depends on what shows up: training, putting a process in order, or building a system.
faq.q3: What if my processes aren't written down anywhere?
faq.a3: That's the most common case. Structuring the process is part of the work — and it comes before any automation. We don't build agents without well-defined processes.
faq.a4: We don't promise savings, sales, or hours: your numbers measure that. We don't hand over a tool and walk away. And our systems don't confirm prices, availability, or terms nobody verified: when they don't know something, they say so, they ask, or they hand the conversation to a person.
faq.a5: We define in writing what information can be used, what gets anonymized, and what stays out. And AI tools do get things wrong sometimes: that's why everything is set up so a person can review and decide.
faq.a6: Training and advisory are quoted per group and per outcome; implementation separately, with scope and success criteria in writing. We don't publish prices because we don't sell packages: every proposal is about your case.

cta.headline: Tell us about your operation.
cta.body: You write to us, a person answers, and we see if there's something worth doing. Sometimes the honest answer is “not yet” — we'll give you that one too.

hero.headline: Diana answers your hotel's WhatsApp at any hour. Diana books for you, and you manage it.
hero.sub: A front desk with artificial intelligence: it answers with your hotel's real information, quotes, builds the complete reservation, confirms it and handles everything before, during and after the stay. Behind it there's a panel where your team sees everything and operates from one place.
hero.nota: Osppy's assistant operates today in hotels in production · On the official WhatsApp API from Meta
hero.ctaMessage: Hi, I'd like to book a demo of Diana for my hotel.

labels.setup: How do you get set up?

root.answer: Hi 👋 I'm Diana, Osppy's assistant for hotels. I live in your hotel's WhatsApp: I answer guests with your information, quote them, build their reservation and follow up until they leave. And I let you know about whatever needs your decision. Ask me anything.

different.answer: I'm not a menu of options. I understand a long message with three questions mixed together and answer all three, in Mexican Spanish or in English if that's what I'm written in. And if something isn't loaded, I say so or ask: I never make up a rate or a policy.

pricing.answer: It's billed monthly, per property. There are different plans depending on how many conversations your hotel has, plus a one-time setup. You'll get the numbers at the demo, with your case in front of you.

night.answer: Yes. At three in the morning on a Sunday I answer the same as on a Tuesday at noon.

setup.answer: You hand us rates, policies, rooms and the questions you get asked most; the Osppy team loads it, registers the templates with Meta and tests everything end to end before going live. It takes days, not weeks.

human.answer: Whenever you want. From the panel you see every conversation, take over, and when you resolve it I pick it back up. And if I detect a complaint or anything sensitive, I hand it to someone on your team right away.

demo.answer: Great. Book a demo and I'll show you how I'd answer at your hotel, with your rates and your policies. A person will take care of you.

problema.headline: Overnight messages go cold. Daytime messages are always the same.
problema.body: A small hotel lives off direct bookings on WhatsApp, and that WhatsApp almost always lives on the phone of whoever runs the place. This is how it sounds from the inside:

r1.titulo: They write at one in the morning
r1.body: “They ask the price and whether breakfast is included, and by the time I answer they've booked somewhere else.”

r2.titulo: Answering the same thing twenty times
r2.body: “Price, breakfast, parking, check-in time. The same thing, all day, at any hour.”

r3.titulo: A number that never switches off
r3.body: “My WhatsApp lives on my personal phone and I can never disconnect. And the direct booking slips away because nobody answered in time.”

hace.headline: Answers with your information. Builds the reservation. You approve.
hace.body: Diana replies on your hotel's WhatsApp with what you loaded: rates, taxes, cancellation policies, breakfast, pets, parking, check-in and check-out times and your frequently asked questions. Whatever isn't loaded, it doesn't make up.

i1.titulo: Quotes and builds the complete reservation
i1.body: Dates, room, number of guests and name, in the same conversation. Multiple rooms or the whole property too, with extra-person charges and taxes as you defined them.

i2.titulo: Hands it to you with a button
i2.body: The built reservation lands on your WhatsApp with two buttons: approve or decline. On approval, Diana sends the guest the deposit details. The room is taken when it's paid, not when it's approved.

i3.titulo: Hands over to a person when it matters
i3.body: Complaints, sensitive requests or anything outside its remit reach your team with a heads-up. From the panel someone answers and resolves it, and Diana picks the conversation back up.

conversacion.m1: Hi, do you have a room for two people from Friday to Sunday? Is breakfast included, and do you have parking?
conversacion.m2: Hi! Yes, for those dates we have a double room for two. Breakfast is included and there's free parking for guests. I'll send you the rate with taxes included, no surprises. Shall I set up the reservation?
conversacion.m3: Yes please. Do you take pets?
conversacion.m4: Yes, small pets with a per-stay fee; I'll include it in the total. To build the reservation I just need your full name.
conversacion.m6: Done, Andrea: double room, Friday to Sunday, two people. I'm passing your reservation to the hotel; as soon as they approve it I'll send you how to make the deposit. Your room is held once the payment comes in.

circuito.headline: Diana does it. You approve with one tap. The panel shows it all.
circuito.sub: Nothing confirms itself. Diana does the work: quotes, builds the reservation, sends the deposit details and confirms with the guest. You manage it: approve and confirm payment with one tap.

telefono.aprobada: Approved. The guest now has the details to transfer.
telefono.pagoConfirmado: Payment confirmed. Diana confirms the reservation with the guest and the room is taken.

funciones.headline: What it does, and what it deliberately doesn't.

f1.body: Rates, taxes, policies, breakfast, pets, parking, schedules and your FAQs: loaded once, in your own words, and that's what Diana answers with.

f2.body: At night and on weekends it answers just like at noon, with the same information and the same tone.

f3.body: Mexican Spanish by default. If the guest writes in English, it answers in English and stays in that language.

f4.body: Approve or decline from your own WhatsApp, without opening anything else. And if two people ask for the same room, whoever pays first keeps it: there are never two paid reservations on the same room.

f5.body: Complaints, sensitive requests or topics outside its remit it doesn't answer: it passes them to your team with a heads-up and picks back up once someone resolves them.

f6.titulo: On the official WhatsApp API from Meta
f6.body: Meta-approved templates, privacy notice on first contact, one-word opt-out, data isolated per business and daily encrypted backups off the server.

widgets.chatA1: Yes, there's a pool for guests. Want me to send photos?

no.n1: It doesn't connect to booking platforms or reservation systems: not today, and with no committed date.
no.n2: It doesn't confirm reservations on its own: it always goes through your button.
no.n3: It doesn't offer discounts or room upgrades on its own initiative.
no.n4: It doesn't replace your team: it takes the repetitive part and leaves them the decisions.

arranque.headline: Days of setup, not weeks of project.
arranque.p1: You give us your information: rates, policies, rooms, amenities and your most repeated conversations, so Diana speaks in your vocabulary from day one.
arranque.p2: Osppy loads the configuration, writes and registers the templates with Meta and tests the full loop.
arranque.p3: We hand you the panel with role-based access and run the kickoff session with your team.
arranque.nota: The clock is set by Meta's verification of your number, not by the setup work.

precio.headline: One structure, no fine print. The figures, on your case.
precio.body: We don't sell flat packages. The real cost of the service is driven by conversation volume, and a flat price ends up degrading the service: we'd rather say so up front.
precio.p1: A monthly fee per property, with a fair-use allowance of conversations included.
precio.p2: Different plans depending on your hotel's number of conversations; you see the volume in the panel.
precio.p3: A one-time setup: loading rooms, policies, FAQs, templates and testing.
precio.p4: Several properties in a single account.
precio.p5: No long contracts. Your data is yours and exportable.
precio.nota: You get the figures at the demo, with your volume and your operation in front of you.

testimonios.nota: Quotes without names and without figures: they illustrate what it's like to have an assistant answering. They are not verified testimonials.
testimonios.q1: I used to answer messages at midnight every single day. Now I sleep. The assistant replies in my tone, with my business's exact information.
testimonios.q2: I thought a bot would feel fake. Not at all: my clients write to it the same way they write to me, and it knows when to hand the conversation over.
testimonios.q3: I stopped losing bookings to slow replies. What comes in overnight no longer goes unanswered.

faq.headline: What a hotel asks us before starting.
faq.q1: What if Diana tells a guest something wrong?
faq.a1: It only answers with what you loaded. If something isn't there, it says so or asks; it never makes up an amenity, a policy or a rate. And it never confirms a reservation on its own: that always goes through your button.
faq.q2: Does it connect to my reservation system or to the platforms?
faq.a2: Not today, and we won't give you a date we can't keep. That's why the lock is you, with the approve buttons: for a small hotel it's the healthiest way.
faq.q3: Do I have to change my WhatsApp number?
faq.a3: You decide. Your current number can move to Diana — it stops working in the phone app and old chats don't migrate — or you use a new one and keep yours as it is. We look at it together based on how you use it today, and the clock is set by Meta's verification.
faq.a4: Diana runs on the official WhatsApp API from Meta, with approved templates. Blocks come from unofficial setups.
faq.q5: Does it replace my front-desk staff?
faq.a5: No, and that's not what we're selling you. It takes away the grind of answering the same thing twenty times a day. The decisions stay yours, and handing the conversation to a person is a permanent part of the design.
faq.q6: What if I want to cancel?
faq.a6: No long contracts. You take your data with you: it's yours and exportable.
